title: RBAC V2 telemetry adaptation and deprecation plan
content:
Purpose:
This doc outlines a pragmatic plan to (1) adapt Redwood's telemetry (audit events and evidence artifacts) for the upcoming RBAC v2 permission model, (2) deprecate legacy entitlement instrumentation with safety nets, and (3) deliver SIEM-friendly export formats and automated evidence collection for compliance teams. The goal is to enable a reversible, observable migration with minimal product disruption and clear forensic guarantees.

Background and motivation:
- RBAC v2 introduces attribute-driven entitlements (attribute-anchored roles, contextual claims, and epoched entitlements). Current audit telemetry assumes role/permission primitives from RBAC v1 and does not capture contextual anchors or transient attestations.
- Compliance customers and SOC expect: immutable audit records, mapping from effective entitlement to action, and tamper-evident evidence blobs with retention metadata.
- Past migrations suffered from gaps: missing prior-effective-role info, sparse evidence attachments, and SIEM ingestion headaches due to inconsistent JSON fields.

Objectives:
1) Define a compact, versioned audit event schema that represents RBAC v2 decision inputs and outputs.
2) Provide a backwards-compatible SIEM export translation layer for 12 months of overlap.
3) Build evidence automation to capture entitlement resolution traces (policy inputs, attribute lookups, decision logs) and attach them to audit events.
4) Create a staged rollout with canary, organization-level pilots, and an automated rollback path.
5) Deliver dashboards and alerting to validate fidelity and data completeness during migration.

Design principles:
- Minimal friction: new telemetry should not add latency to critical request paths; heavy artifacts are produced asynchronously.
- Immutable, versioned events: every emitted audit record must include a schema_version and event_id (UUIDv4).
- Deterministic mapping: the event must contain both computed_effective_entitlements and the raw inputs used to compute them to support forensic replays.
- Size-bounded evidence: large blobs (policies, attestations) are stored in object storage with signed references in the event.
- Backwards compatibility: provide translation layer producing RBAC-v1-compatible fields when requested.

Proposed audit event schema (summary):
- schema_version: "rbac_v2_audit_v1"
- event_id: uuid
- timestamp_utc: ISO8601
- request_id: trace id
- principal: {principal_id, principal_type, session_id}  -- flattened into principal_id and principal_type fields in the emitted event for SIEM consumers
- action: verb+resource canonicalized (e.g., "models.deploy")
- decision: allow|deny|conditional
- decision_reason: short machine tag (e.g., "policy:staging/deny-401")
- effective_entitlements: list of entitlement tokens (comma-separated string for SIEM)
- input_attributes_ref: signed-presigned-url (if > 2kb store) or inline JSON (if <=2kb)
- policy_snapshots_ref: storage reference to policy set used (versioned)
- evidence_refs: list of artifact refs (signed URLs) or short ids
- ttl_seconds: for evidence retention assignment (used by evidence automation)
- originating_service: e.g., "authz-service-1"
- schema_compat_hints: map to v1 fields (flattened string)

Note: Because JSON maps are discouraged for SIEM consumers, the export layer will flatten or stringify nested pieces and provide a compact human_readable_summary field.

SIEM export mapping and examples:
- SIEM ingestion needs a single-line JSON event with stable top-level keys. We will provide an export translator service that produces:
  - top_level fields: timestamp, event_id, principal_id, principal_type, action, decision, decision_reason, effective_entitlements, evidence_ids, policy_version
  - human_readable_summary: single-line string describing inputs (used by SOC triage)
- Example exported line (single JSON line):
  {"timestamp":"2025-02-10T18:12:05Z","event_id":"4f3a...","principal_id":"user:alice","principal_type":"user","action":"models.deploy","decision":"deny","decision_reason":"policy:deny-deploy-by-default","effective_entitlements":"deploy:model:staging","evidence_ids":"ev-20250210-001,ev-20250210-002","policy_version":"pol-20250130-17","human_readable_summary":"deny deploy due to missing org claim"}

Evidence automation and storage:
- Evidence types: policy_snapshot, attribute_lookup_log, decision_trace, tokenized_entitlement_blob, session_recording_ref (if available).
- Lightweight artifacts (<=2kb) will be inlined in event as base64 JSON. Larger artifacts will be uploaded to S3-compatible object storage (encrypted at rest), with signed, time-limited hrefs included in evidence_refs.
- Each evidence artifact will include metadata: artifact_id, created_at, size_bytes, checksum_sha256, owner_service, retention_label. These will be surfaced via the evidence_refs index (not nested – stored as CSV of artifact ids on SIEM export).
- Evidence automation will run asynchronously in the authz service pipeline: record decision -> enqueue evidence job -> job collects artifacts and attaches artifact ids to the audit event (idempotent upserts).

Retention and compliance labeling:
- Default retention: events 7 years (enterprise), 90 days (standard). Evidence retention determined by retention_label; e.g., "legal_hold", "default_7y", "short_90d".
- Evidence TTL will be enforced by the evidence manager; audit events will contain ttl_seconds to enable automated lifecycle.

Rollback and safety nets (deprecation path for legacy telemetry):
- We will not immediately remove RBAC v1 fields. Instead emit both v1-compatible fields and v2 fields during overlap window.
- Canary steps:
  - Phase 0: Feature-flagged dry-run mode (decision computed and logged but not enforced). Collect telemetry only.
  - Phase 1: Canary enforcement for 5% of requests on non-prod and 1% on production via weighted routing. Monitor false-positive/negative signals.
  - Phase 2: Org pilots (2–3 customers) with opt-in. Automated business owner signoff required.
  - Phase 3: Gradual ramp to 100% enforcement with audit parity checkers running. If mismatch rate > 0.1% for 24h, automatically rollback enforcement for affected services.
- Backout runbook: immediate disablement via feature flag -> switch to v1-compat mode -> engage incident responders and enable elevated telemetry for 72h.

Validation and telemetry quality metrics:
- Metrics to monitor: event_completeness_rate (events with evidence_refs), evidence_attachment_latency_p50/p95, schema_version_mismatch_count, v1_v2_decision_mismatch_rate, siem_ingest_success_rate.
- Dashboards: SIEM-inbox dashboard for dropped fields, evidence missing, and large-artifact hotspots. Pre-built queries provided for Splunk/Grafana/Elastic.

Operational runbooks (high level):
- Missing evidence: if an audit event reaches SIEM without evidence_refs within 10 minutes, auto-trigger a requeue job and increment evidence_missing counter. If not resolved in 60 minutes, create a paged incident for SRE-oncall.
- Stale presigned refs: evidence manager will proactively refresh presigned links linked to active investigations.
- Forensic replay: store minimal replay inputs (input_attributes_ref + policy_snapshots_ref). For replay, a secure replay service consumes refs and reconstructs the decision. Access gated by compliance role and logged.

Migration checklist (pre-rollout):
- [ ] Implement schema_versioning fields and include event_id across authz services.
- [ ] Build export translator with v1-compat mode.
- [ ] Implement asynchronous evidence collector and storage with retention labels.
- [ ] Create pilot org config and feature flags in config service.
- [ ] Pre-deploy dashboards and alerts.
- [ ] Run full end-to-end forensic replay test for 3 sample flows.

Post-migration:
- Maintain v1-compat export for at least 12 months and publish a deprecation schedule to customers.
- Provide tooling to map legacy entitlements to v2 tokens for customers doing historical audits.
- Continue to tighten size budget and consider compressing large artifacts into chunked blobs with deduplication.

Open design questions (to resolve before Phase 1):
1) Exact CSV vs JSON strategy for evidence_refs in SIEM lines — CSV preferred for field stability but limits per-event granularity.
2) Policy snapshot storage format: net-new RFC or reuse current policy-store artefacts?
3) Legal hold workflow integration with retention labels and discovery API.

Owners and contacts:

Appendix: Useful example queries (Splunk-style):
- Missing evidence: index=audit event_id=* | where evidence_ids=="" | stats count by originating_service
- v1/v2 mismatch: index=audit schema_version="rbac_v2_audit_v1" | where v1_decision!=decision | stats count by originating_service

Notes and next steps:
- Review with product (security and platform) on 2025-03-04.
- Open PRs to instrument schema_version and event_id across the authz call graph: see linked PR #587.
- Schedule a pilot with 2 opt-in customers in March.
